correctness.rationale: The identity \(27X(t)^2+343Z(t)^2=250Y(t)^2\) is an exact integer-polynomial equality; a quartic difference is strictly positive for all \(t\ge2\). The explicitly computed Sylvester resultant has only prime factors 2,3,5,7,13, and reduction to t=1 mod 2730 rules out every common prime of the first two terms. Oddness and A+C=2B force pairwise coprimality. CRT residues impose exact valuations (3,2) on each of the three terms, proving powerful but non-perfect-power status for infinitely many distinct t. Minimality follows from exhaustive exact factorization of all integers ≤57967, leading to 186 Achilles numbers and precisely the triple (14283,36125,57967) in the complete gcd-filtered pair enumeration. The standalone stdlib verifier independently reconstructs identities, resultant, CRT and finite enumeration. No finite test is used as proof of infinitude.

value.rationale: The published study of primitive powerful arithmetic progressions leaves open the structurally stricter case where no term is a perfect power. The new theorem provides infinitely many explicitly parameterized pairwise-coprime all-Achilles progressions, and determines the first possible primitive three-term progression exactly. This natural boundary between perfect-power constructions and genuinely non-perfect-power squarefull entries is not a routine normalization of an existing square construction. The least-term invariant is motivated by the same progression problem and certified by a mathematically complete finite check.
